correspondence.body:
Dear Brothers,

Thank you for submitting the S-51 form.

Can you please now submit the following documents as mentioned in paragraph 5 of the Instructions for Recommending New Congregations (S-50):

• Coordinator of the Body of Elders/Secretary Change of Address (S-29)
• Kingdom Hall Information (S-5)
• Periodical Request (M-202)
• Shipping Information (S-36)
• Territory Adjustment Request (S-6)

Once you have completed these forms, please send them to me.

As a side note, please forward the body’s recommendation(s) for COBE as soon as possible, as I will need to appoint a coordinator for the new congregation if it is approved. SFG 1:11, 12

Thank you for your hard work, brothers.

Warm regards,
Daniel Martin
Circuit NZ-1

organisation.scope_note: This is a planning register, not an appointment record. Confirmed names are based on the user’s instruction. All other entries remain to be decided by the body of elders or the responsible appointing brother according to current direction. Eligibility badges show whether a ministerial servant may be considered; they do not approve or appoint anyone.

legend.label: A qualified ministerial servant may be assigned
A qualified ministerial servant may be used only when the stated need or current direction applies
This chart treats the role as an elder assignment

notes: For field service groups, an elder is a group overseer; when there are not enough elders, a qualified ministerial servant may serve as group servant or group assistant (SFG 1:21).
For auxiliary counselor, an experienced elder should be used whenever possible; the conditional badge flags that an MS should not be treated as the normal choice (SFG 4:15).
A Kingdom Hall Operating Committee may include elders or ministerial servants, but its coordinator should be an experienced elder (SFG 13:6).
Secretary support means assistance with field-service reporting tasks under the secretary, not appointment as the congregation secretary (SFG 1:14).

oversight.title: Oversight and Responsibility View
oversight.principle: The body of elders provides collective spiritual oversight. The coordinator helps the body work in an orderly way but is not the coordinator of the congregation and does not independently direct the other elders.
oversight.appointment_note: The circuit overseer appoints the coordinator of the body of elders (SFG 1:11).

regular_pioneer_review.title: Regular Pioneer Hour Review and Shepherding Guide
regular_pioneer_review.confidentiality_note: The controlling Shepherd material is confidential. Keep this derived working topic within the authorised elders’ project and do not circulate it as a public policy statement.
regular_pioneer_review.authority_note: This is a paraphrased working aid based on the September 2025 Shepherd edition and the public Organized book. Check the current Shepherd Addendum, JW Hub instructions and Branch direction before acting.
regular_pioneer_review.bottom_line: Do not begin by asking a pioneer to step down. First verify the record, understand the person’s circumstances and offer help. A total below 560 hours at service-year end requires a prompt, balanced Congregation Service Committee determination; it is not automatic deletion. If discontinuation is best, present it as a potentially temporary, stress-relieving adjustment—not as discipline or a judgment of spiritual worth.

thresholds.meaning: An applicant should have organised personal affairs so the annual requirement can realistically be reached.

thresholds.value: Consistently below an average of 50 hours per month
thresholds.meaning: After factoring in hour credit, the service overseer and group overseer meet with the pioneer to offer assistance and assess whether the annual requirement is realistic.
Hours in field service plus applicable hour credit; the pioneer may continue.
The Service Committee promptly decides whether the pioneer should continue, using balanced judgment. This is not an automatic deletion rule.

decision_flow.title: Verify the record
actions: Confirm the service year and months appointed
Reconcile reported field-service hours
Confirm properly recorded hour credit
Check for missing or late reports
Identify approved theocratic-project work that may require special consideration

decision_flow.title: Meet to understand and assist
actions: The service overseer and appropriate group overseer meet with the pioneer
Commend specific faithful service
Ask about health, family, employment, schedule and other circumstances
Offer practical help before discussing discontinuation
Assess whether the new service year’s requirement is realistically sustainable

decision_flow.title: Check special provisions
actions: Consider approved-project special consideration
Consider the rare infirm-pioneer provision only if all criteria may apply
Consult the circuit overseer where the infirm provision requires it
Check the current Addendum and JW Hub direction
decision_flow.owner: Congregation Service Committee / Body of elders

decision_flow.title: Make a balanced determination
actions: Consider the length of full-time service
Consider age and whether circumstances are temporary or continuing
Consider the pioneer’s best interests
Uphold the standard for regular pioneer service
Do not leave a below-560 case unresolved or place the burden on the pioneer to volunteer a resignation

decision_flow.title: Communicate and record the outcome
actions: Update the body of elders before an announcement
If discontinuing, two Service Committee members inform the individual first
Use the current JW Hub process
Use only the prescribed announcement
Record special or infirm consideration on S-21 when applicable

exceptions.title: Approved-project special consideration
exceptions.criteria: The pioneer missed the annual requirement because extensive work on approved theocratic projects exceeded the hour credit available.
exceptions.outcome: The pioneer may continue, should be warmly commended and has the special consideration noted on S-21.

exceptions.title: Infirm regular pioneer
exceptions.criteria: Rare provision: exemplary, over 50 years old, at least 15 cumulative years pioneering and a heartfelt desire to continue; the circuit overseer must be consulted.
exceptions.outcome: If the body approves, the pioneer may serve without an hour requirement; two Service Committee members explain the provision and it is noted on S-21.

exceptions.title: Ordinary changed circumstances
exceptions.criteria: Health, employment, family responsibilities or another adverse circumstance makes the annual requirement unrealistic but does not meet a special provision.
exceptions.outcome: Temporary discontinuation may be in the person’s best interests and relieve pressure until circumstances change.

principles: Use the meeting to listen and assist, not to announce a predetermined outcome.
Separate the privilege of regular pioneering from the person’s spirituality and value to Jehovah or the congregation.
Use verified figures without accusatory expressions such as ‘you failed to make your time.’
Do not pressure the pioneer to chase an unsafe or unrealistic deficit.
If discontinuation is considered, use the official idea of discontinuing for a time rather than the status-oriented expression ‘step down.’
questions: How have you been, and what circumstances affected your ministry during the service year?
Is any report or approved hour credit missing from the record?
What practical assistance could the elders or congregation provide?
Looking at your present circumstances, is reaching the annual requirement during the new service year realistic?
Would a workable adjustment make continuation sustainable, or would discontinuing for a time relieve pressure until circumstances change?
conversation.sample_opening: We appreciate your service and want this to be an encouraging conversation, not a disciplinary one. Your value to Jehovah and the congregation is not measured by a title or a number of hours. We would first like to understand what affected your service, confirm that the record is accurate and see what practical help we can offer. Then we can consider together whether continuing regular pioneer service is realistic in your present circumstances.

ashburton_transfer.current_owner: Until 1 November 2026, the pioneer remains under the current congregation, so that congregation’s Service Committee should resolve the completed service-year review.
ashburton_transfer.transfer_requirement: The letter of introduction should plainly state whether the existing body recommends that the pioneer continue.
ashburton_transfer.new_congregation_action: If the recommendation is favourable, the new Ashburton Tagalog Congregation Service Committee confirms that the pioneer wishes to continue and, absent an exceptional reason, arranges the announcement at the next midweek meeting.

preparation_meeting.title: Informal Congregation Preparation Meeting
preparation_meeting.purpose: Prepare the Ashburton Tagalog Congregation to begin functioning on 1 November 2026 by identifying proposed role assignments, assigning preparation work and surfacing decisions that require formal approval or Branch direction.
preparation_meeting.authority_note: This is a preparation meeting, not a body-of-elders meeting. Record proposed names and action owners. Formal appointments, congregation decisions, shared-hall decisions and external legal or banking actions must be made or confirmed by the authorised brothers or body under current direction.

agenda.discussion: Prayer; restate the 1 November start date and the purpose of tonight’s discussion.
agenda.outcome: Everyone understands what may be prepared, proposed or formally decided.

agenda.discussion: Approval received; congregation 3814 in Circuit NZ-2; Adamson dela Cruz confirmed as coordinator and Dave Asuncion as secretary; review the Branch transition instructions without circulating confidential material.
agenda.outcome: One shared understanding of the approved identity, effective date and current arrangement.

agenda.discussion: Work through the priority role table: service overseer, meeting oversight, accounts, literature, territory, field service groups, cleaning and shared-hall liaison.
agenda.outcome: A proposed name or a named follow-up owner for every priority vacancy.

agenda.discussion: First-month schedule; public talks; Life and Ministry assignments; Watchtower conductor and substitute; chairmen, readers, A/V and attendants; confirm Thursday 7:15 p.m. and Saturday 7:00 p.m.
agenda.outcome: Owners and target dates for the first four weeks of meeting schedules and rosters.

agenda.discussion: Field service group structure; publisher placements; interim S-6 territory; literature and periodical requests; pioneer and publisher-record transition after 1 November.
agenda.outcome: Proposed group structure and named owners for territory, literature and record reconciliation.

agenda.topic: Administration, JW Hub and Kingdom Hall
agenda.discussion: JW Hub access; secure congregation file; S-21/S-88 records; information board; cleaning schedule; emergency contacts; S-46 shared-hall matters and Kingdom Hall Operating Committee liaison.
agenda.outcome: Administrative setup tasks assigned, with any combined-body decisions clearly flagged.

agenda.topic: Optional: charity, tax, bank and accounting preparation
agenda.discussion: Confirm that Branch Accounting/Legal direction is needed first; identify who will obtain current S-27 and clarify the legal entity/account name; list—but do not yet execute—bank onboarding and conditional charity/IRD steps.
agenda.outcome: One inquiry owner and a document-gathering owner; no unauthorised registration or account opening.

agenda.discussion: Read back every action with owner and due date; identify what goes to the host body, prospective/new body, combined bodies, circuit overseer or Branch; set the next preparation review.
agenda.outcome: A complete action register and date for the next review.

discussion_questions: Which roles absolutely need a named brother before the first meeting, and which can be covered temporarily?
Do the proposed brothers have the availability, ability and eligibility indicated in the organisation chart?
Who has formal authority to confirm each proposal, and by what date should that confirmation be obtained?
How many field service groups should begin on 1 November, and who will care for each group?
Who will prepare and check the first four weeks of meeting, ministry and Kingdom Hall rosters?
What records, access, supplies or information must come from Ashburton or other former congregations?
What must be agreed with the other bodies using the Kingdom Hall?
Who will contact Branch Accounting/Legal for the legal-entity and bank-account instructions?
preparation_meeting.optional_finance_note: Discuss only enough to assign preparation work. Do not create an entity, register with Charities Services, apply for an IRD number or open an account under an assumed name before Branch Accounting/Legal identifies the approved arrangement. Obtain the current S-27 before designing the accounting workflow.

startup.legal_control: Do not independently create a charitable trust, register a charity, obtain a new IRD number, or open an account under an assumed entity. First obtain written direction from the branch Accounting/Legal function identifying the legal entity, official account name, tax/charity identifiers, governing documents and authorised banking process for congregation 3814.
startup.short_version: Before 1 November, complete the announcement, leadership, JW Hub, accounting, shared-hall, meeting and ministry setup. On or shortly after 1 November, transfer people and records, confirm pioneers and appointed brothers, and begin congregation records. After November, submit the first field service report and operate the monthly accounting and compliance routines. Charity registration is conditional on branch direction; bank-account preparation may begin now, but the legal account holder must be confirmed first.

gates.meaning: Explicitly required by the approval letter or another cited official instruction.
Needed so the congregation can function cleanly from the start, even if the approval letter does not list it.
Do not execute until the branch or other named authority confirms the exact arrangement.
Complete on or after 1 November, or during the first reporting cycle.

phases.title: A. Before 1 November — establish control and readiness
phases.purpose: These items give the new body a functioning decision structure, secure records, meeting arrangements and ministry support before the effective date.

items.title: Read page 1 of the approval letter at the first midweek meeting after receipt.
items.detail: Do not read the confidential postscript.

items.title: Post page 1 of the approval letter on the information board after the announcement.
items.detail: The coordinator approves information-board content.

items.title: Secure the confidential postscript and limit it to those authorised to use it.
items.detail: Do not read or post page 2.

items.title: Complete the Congregation Service Committee.
items.detail: Adamson dela Cruz and Dave Asuncion are confirmed; the service overseer remains to be confirmed.

items.title: Assign the essential congregation roles and rosters.
items.detail: Prioritise accounts, literature, territory, meeting oversight, public talks, A/V, attendants, field service groups and cleaning; use the organisation chart as the working register.

items.title: Prepare the new JW Hub domain and access transition.
items.detail: Confirm the coordinator and secretary can see the new domain during the branch transition window.

items.title: Obtain and review the current Instructions for Congregation Use of JW Hub (S-135).
items.detail: Use it for access, person transfers, official correspondence and record handling.

items.title: Create a secure congregation file and its required categories.
items.detail: Accounts; circuit overseer reports; confidential records; elders and ministerial servants; Kingdom Hall; letters of introduction; territory.

items.title: Update the shared Kingdom Hall Agreement (S-46).
items.detail: Record meeting times, use and care, each congregation’s operating-expense responsibility, operating-account balance and extraordinary-expense limits.

items.title: Publish the first month of meeting assignments and support rosters.
items.detail: Include chairmen, readers, A/V, attendants, talks, Life and Ministry parts and approved substitutes; verify the approved Thursday 7:15 p.m. and Saturday 7:00 p.m. times.

items.title: Establish field service groups and ministry support.
items.detail: Assign publishers, group overseers/servants and assistants; prepare territory and literature handling.

items.title: Prepare congregation emergency contacts and shared-hall safety procedures.
items.detail: Apply privacy safeguards; know the current security, incident and life-safety direction.
items.owner: Body of elders / Kingdom Hall Operating Committee

phases.title: B. Legal, charity, tax and banking — confirm the structure first
phases.purpose: The account and accounting system are operational needs. Separate legal-entity, charity and tax registrations are conditional because the available branch letter and S-50 do not instruct this congregation to register independently.

items.title: Ask the branch Accounting/Legal function to identify the approved legal and banking structure for congregation 3814.
items.detail: Confirm whether the congregation uses an existing nationwide entity/registration or needs any separate local entity; obtain the exact legal name, IRD/charity identifiers and process in writing.

items.title: Obtain and review the current Instructions for Congregation Accounting (S-27) and tutorial videos.
items.detail: Treat S-27 as the controlling accounting checklist; this project does not have a current local copy.

items.title: Appoint and train the accounts servant.
items.detail: The secretary oversees the work; the coordinator arranges audits.

items.title: Approve and minute the bank-account resolution.
items.detail: Use the exact branch-approved legal/account name, address, account operators and authorisations. Have the number of signers and approval controls match S-27.

items.title: Assemble the bank onboarding pack.
items.detail: Expect entity or registration evidence if applicable, recent signed minutes, authorised-person identity/address verification and tax-residency information; follow the selected bank’s current checklist.

items.title: Open and verify the congregation bank account and online access.
items.detail: Test deposits, authorised payments, statements and handover access before relying on it; do not receive funds under an assumed entity name.

items.title: Set up the congregation accounting records and approved payment/donation workflow.
items.detail: Record opening balances, statement cycle, approvals, reports, receipts and secure retention exactly as directed by S-27.

items.title: Schedule the first congregation accounts audit and future audit cycle.
items.detail: Record who will audit, the period covered and where the report will be filed.

items.title: Only if directed, complete the approved entity/Charities Services registration path.
items.detail: Use branch-approved rules and officers. Charities Services registration is voluntary generally and is not established here as a separate start condition; current applications may take up to 20 weeks.
references: Companies Office if incorporation is directed

items.title: Only if directed, complete the correct IRD, donee-status and tax setup.
items.detail: If registering with Charities Services, do not separately apply for an IRD number; Inland Revenue says it supplies one after registration. Otherwise use the route specified for the approved entity.

phases.title: C. On or shortly after 1 November — activate the congregation
phases.purpose: These transfers and confirmations take effect when congregation 3814 begins functioning, not while the Tagalog group remains under the host congregation.

items.title: Receive letters of introduction and S-21 records from former congregations.
items.detail: Former secretaries send them on or shortly after 1 November.

items.title: Receive Congregation Persons transfers in JW Hub.
items.detail: Reconcile every expected publisher with the proposed list and investigate omissions or duplicates.

items.title: Submit S-62 recommendations for elders and ministerial servants who transfer.
items.detail: No S-62 is needed for the brothers assigned as coordinator and secretary.

items.title: Review and confirm transferred regular pioneers.
items.detail: Check the introduction-letter recommendation, confirm each pioneer wishes to continue and announce favourable confirmations at the next midweek meeting.

items.title: Make the authorised appointment and pioneer announcements at the proper time.
items.detail: Do not announce prospective assignments before they are effective or confirmed under current direction.

items.title: Put the interim territory arrangement into operation.
items.detail: Use the boundaries submitted with S-6 until updated territory assignments arrive; create controlled territory records and assignments.

items.title: Activate literature, periodical, workbook and shipping arrangements.
items.detail: Verify the M-202 request, literature handling and the S-36/Kingdom Hall Literature Group arrangement; avoid duplicate orders during the handover.

items.title: Begin separate S-88 attendance and S-21 publisher records for the new congregation.
items.detail: Use the electronic or printed method decided by the body and preserve confidentiality.

phases.title: D. First month and ongoing — prove the system works
phases.purpose: Close the launch by completing the first reports, testing routines and recording all recurring obligations.

items.title: Submit the congregation’s first field service report after the end of November.
items.detail: Reconcile publisher reports first; the general monthly deadline in SFG is no later than the 20th.

items.title: Complete and review the first monthly congregation accounts report.
items.detail: Confirm statement reconciliation, approvals, target balance and filing under the current S-27.
items.owner: Accounts Servant / Secretary / Body of elders

items.title: Establish the new congregation’s controlled information-board routine.
items.detail: Coordinator approval is required; post only congregation-activity information and the current cleaning schedule.

items.title: Run the first cleaning cycle and confirm supplies and safety instructions.
items.detail: Coordinate with the shared-hall operating committee; post the schedule.

items.title: Confirm the congregation’s participation in the shared Kingdom Hall operating arrangement.
items.detail: The combined bodies appoint the operating committee; record the new congregation’s representative, expenses and communication route.

items.title: Hold a 30-day launch review.
items.detail: Reconcile people, appointments, meetings, ministry, territory, literature, bank/accounting, hall use and unresolved correspondence; assign corrective actions.

items.title: Create the recurring compliance and review calendar.
items.detail: Include monthly reports/accounts, audits, January file review, hall/agreement reviews and—only if the approved entity is separately registered—Charities Services annual return within six months of balance date and change notifications.
